newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends slightly down, gilts recoup losses.
newsitem.headline: India call ends slightly down, gilts recoup losses.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday around 4.0 percent, marginally down from opening quotes of 4.0-4.25 percent but off the day's low of 3.5 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done between 3.5 and 4.0 percent.
"Rates dipped to 3.5 percent late in the morning but firmed up again in the afternoon on some late demand," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Call money was largely steady through the day and rates were range-bound between 3.5 and 4.0 percent," he said.
Tuesday's announcement of an auction of four-year bonds worth 50 billion rupees for July 28 did not have much impact on call money, dealers said.

"Liquidity in the banking system is good and market players do not see it being affected much by the auction," said a dealer. "Rates may firm up a bit next week but we do not see them going up much above 5.0 percent."
Dealers said call money will continue to trade in a 3.5-4.0 percent range on Thursday.
Prices of government securities ended Wednesday up from lows hit on Tuesday after the announcement of the auction but did not rise above levels reached earlier in the day.

"Gilts were up today but did not cross Tuesday's highs," said a dealer. "Prices fell yesterday evening after the bond auction was announced but it seems it was some kind of reflex action by a few market players."
"Sentiment was bullish once again today but I think trade will be cautious till the auction is over," he said.
Dealers said most of Wednesday's trade was in stocks with maturities up to 2004.
The most popular stocks remained the 12.59 percent 2004, 11.83 percent 2003 and the 12.14 percent 2000, dealers said.

The 12.59 percent 2004 traded at 104.51 rupees against Tuesday's highest traded 104.30, the 11.83 percent 2003 changed hands at 101.25 against 101.30 while the 12.14 percent 2000 rose to 104.32 from 104.30, dealers said.
Among treasury bills, the 364-day bill yielded 7.5 percent against 7.6, dealers said.
